The S&P 500 fell to its 3-year low as traders became increasingly cautious ahead of Nvidia's earnings report, which failed to impress and sparked concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence on the economy.

S&P 500 (-2.24% to 7014.81): S&P 500 Falls to 3-Year Low. The S&P 500 fell 2.24% to 7014.81, marking its lowest level since 2020, as traders watched Nvidia's earnings release, which dragged down AI-related stocks. The Nasdaq also fell, extending its slide to its third day, as investors became increasingly cautious ahead of the tech giant's results. The market's decline was seen as a sign of growing concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence on the economy.
Nasdaq (-3.68% to 23000.02): Nasdaq Falls on Nvidia Earnings Concerns. Nasdaq fell 3.68% to 23000.02 as investors became increasingly nervous about Nvidia's earnings report, which failed to impress. The Dow also slipped, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq extended their losses. Traders are watching for signs of a slowdown in the tech sector, which has been a key driver of the market's recent gains.

USD/JPY (-0.33% to 158.85): USD/JPY Sell-Off. The USD/JPY pair fell 0.33% to 158.85 as traders reacted to a slowdown in the dollar's rally, which was fueled by the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hikes. The yen's relative strength was boosted by lower US yields and a looming interest rate hike by the Bank of Japan, according to FXStreet [12]. This trend was also echoed by Bloomberg.com, which reported that the yen's safe-haven status was enhanced by an AI selloff, drawing demand from investors seeking haven assets [14].
Crude Oil (-0.3% to 82.96): Oil Prices Fall Amid Supply Concerns. Crude oil prices fell due to concerns about a global supply surplus, with traders watching the impact of increased Middle East exports and rising US inventory levels. [15] [16] [18] The market is also responding to the news that US oil drillers are increasing production, which could further boost supply. [17]
Gold (-4.49% to 3520.1): Gold's 4.49% Drop. Gold fell 4.49% to 3520.1 as investors became increasingly bearish on the metal, citing a strong US dollar and rising interest rates, which are making gold less attractive as a safe-haven asset. [21] CNBC's report that gold's price keeps falling despite weaker economic data suggests that traders are watching the Fed's tightening cycle and its impact on gold prices. [19]
